report:
Reviewed the complete product_boundaries claim, its ordinary TcxDb association and the sole TODO test. Requirements: identity enumeration, signatures, impl headers and individual associated values are distinct tracked semantic products; consumers enumerate identities before selecting details; external function bodies are unavailable to checking. Captured metadata design and the linked architectural-foundations cross-item-interface rationale.

TcxDb exposes separate module_children/associated_items identity inventories, trait/function/ADT signature products, relevant_trait_impls candidate identities, impl_signature headers, and associated_type_value keyed by both impl and associated definition identity. RawAssociatedItems contains names/kinds/identities/completeness rather than checked function signatures or bodies. RawRelevantImpls similarly contains identities/completeness. RawImplSignature contains generic header/predicate facts, not member values. RawAssociatedTypeValue supplies one requested value. Function signatures contain declaration/owner/receiver/parameter facts but no body product. The trait has no external function body API; macro-expansion APIs return expanded source for their separate purpose, not external function bodies for checking.

Captured external_syms.rs establishes the tracked Sage lowering boundaries which the provider trait alone does not establish: external_trait_items, external_fn_signature, external_trait_signature, external_adt_signature, external_relevant_impls, external_impl_signature and external_associated_type_value are separate tracked queries. Trait item enumeration lowers identities without loading the owner's signature; function detail is requested separately. The associated-value query is keyed by selected impl and associated type. Its lowerer currently also reopens the selected impl signature to obtain binder information; this is a dependency on the selected header, not a scan of sibling values. Existing provider_fact_reuse TODO explicitly reserves provider-owned per-fact invalidation and self-contained associated-value binder facts. Separate tracked semantic lowering is present; dynamic independently mutable provider inputs are not claimed implemented by this review.

Captured ProxyTcxDb/TcxRequest represent these operations as separate channel requests and record their keys. Captured method lookup first asks for trait item identities, filters matching function names, then obtains owner/function signatures only for viable matching candidates. Captured solver candidate assembly requests trait/head-relevant impl identities before their headers. Captured prepared associated-value loading separately requests the chosen candidate's single associated value using its impl and associated identity and copies it with the already-established parameter mapping. These source paths substantiate decomposition while not replacing an end-to-end negative-dependency trace for every consumer.

The sole test todo::metadata_product_boundaries contains no assertions. It explicitly defers method/proof/normalization traces showing identity enumeration followed by selected signatures, applicable headers or the requested associated value, excluding siblings, unrelated impls and all bodies. Completing it requires source-backed external fixtures and observations of provider and semantic query events, with multiple sibling members/impls so absence assertions are meaningful; warm/relevant-edit scenarios must respect the separate provider invalidation TODO. No ordinary behavioral test is associated with this claim, so this review does not claim full runtime demand verification from source layout or annotation alone. No N/A evidence applies.

Commands executed: fresh cargo meta review start with coordinator instructions, source and full-test inspection, review read captures of design/RFD, external tracked lowering, proxy protocol and method/candidate/value consumer excerpts. No tests or build executed by this reviewer; central suite results are separate evidence. No source edits or new suspected behavioral defect. No requested edits; existing demand-trace and provider-fact limitations remain explicit.
